brief: TS Lombard modestly trims high-beta risk exposure (EM equities, industrial metals) but stays overweight risk assets, holding 12m portfolio beta at 1.13. The cut follows oil back above $100/bbl on Hormuz tanker disruption and Saudi pipeline damage, surging global bond yields, the Fed's first hike (delivered hawkishly by Chairman Warsh, three more hikes priced over the next 12 months), and EPS expectations already elevated enough to leave little room for upside surprise. Resilient macro data, a possible Trump war offramp, and a structural AI tailwind keep the firm from cutting more aggressively. It rotates proceeds into leveraged credit, precious metals and managed futures, funded by cuts to EM equities, India (taken to zero) and Italian BTPs. India is cut entirely: AI threatens its back-office export model, high energy prices squeeze its currency and financial conditions, El Nino threatens rainfall, and valuations stay rich at 19x forward earnings. Taiwan remains the sole EM equity overweight and Tech stays overweight on early-stage agentic AI adoption the firm expects to structurally boost EPS. In Europe, French budget conflict and Italian coalition risk widen OAT-Bund and BTP-Bund spreads even as the ECB turns more hawkish.
